In Non-Logged In Reservation flow, when the user enters an input in First Name(Kana) and Last Name(Kana) field and then erases all inputs from the field, the error message “Only katakana characters are allowed” persists on screen.　

While this error message persists on screen, the user is unable to confirm their reservation even if the Kana fields are blank.

Since in Non-Logged In Reservation flow the First Name(Kana) and Last Name(Kana) fields are OPTIONAL, it is expected that if the fields are blank, it should return to its original state (white box) without the error message being displayed and the user is allowed to confirm their reservation.



Preconditions:

a. Ensure user is logged out from Tokyu Stay.



Steps to Reproduce:

# Open [https://stg.reservation.tokyustay.co.jp/en|https://stg.reservation.tokyustay.co.jp/en]
# Select any Hotel > Select any Check-in/Check-out time > Search > Select “Book Now” on any room/plan.
# In the First Name(Kana) or Last Name(Kana) fields, enter any input.
# Erase all inputs from the First Name(Kana) and Last Name(Kana) fields.
# Enter valid inputs in all other fields and attempt to click the “Confirm” button.



Current Result:

Error message persists even after users erases all inputs from First Name(Kana) and Last Name(Kana) fields, which prevents user from confirming reservation



Expected Result:

Error message disappears after users erases all inputs from First Name(Kana) and Last Name(Kana) fields, and allows the user to confirm their reservation.

When the user uses their points to make a reservation, the Point Usage is split into multiple records when displayed on Smart Club even though it is all part of the same reservation.

Similarly, when a user cancels a reservation where they used their points, the Point Rollback split into multiple records when displayed on Smart Club

It is observed that the more points the user used for the reservation, the higher the number of multiple records displayed on Smart Club.



Preconditions:

a. Ensure user has at least 100 points in account



Steps to Reproduce:

# Open [https://stg.reservation.tokyustay.co.jp/en|https://stg.reservation.tokyustay.co.jp/en] > Login
# Select any Hotel > Select any check-in/check-out date > Search > Select “Book Now” on any room/plan
# Enter and use at least 100 points in the “Point Usage” field to deduct the total booking price. > Complete the reservation
# Go to Bookings > Click on the reservation made in Step 4 > Cancel the reservation
# Go to Point Information > Click “Link to My Page” >  Click “ポイント履歴を見る / View Point History” button
# Observe the Point Usage and Point Rollback records for the latest reservation.



Current Result:

"Points Usage" and "Point Rollback" for the same reservation is split into multiple records in Smart Club Point History screen.



Expected Result:

"Points Usage" and "Point Rollback" for the same reservation is shown as a single record in Smart Club Point History screen.

When the user cancels a reservation, the points that they would have earned from the reservation are displayed as the “Returned Points” in the Cancel Reservation modal, regardless of whether the user used points for discount or not.

# Select any Hotel > Select any check-in/check-out time > Search > “Book Now” on any room/plan
# At the Reservation Confirmation screen, take note of the “Points to be Earned” value.
# Click “Confirm” and complete the reservation.
# Go to Bookings > Upcoming Tab > Select the reservation made in Step 4 > Click “Cancel”
# Click “Yes, Cancel” and observe the “Returned Points” value in the Cancel Reservation complete modal.



Current Result:

"Points to be Earned" value is displayed as the "Returned Points" in Cancel Reservation modal



Expected Result:

“Returned Points” value shows the value of the points the user used for the reservation. If no points were used, it displays as 0 points.

In the Edit Profile screen, when the user’s page language is set to either *TC, SC or KR* and the user’s country is set to *Japan*, entering any value that is not Katakana characters (such as *alphabets, numbers, special characters or Hiragana characters*) into the First Name(Kana) and Last Name(Kana) fields, the user is given an error message to “Please enter your first/last name” for the respective languages.

The expected behavior is that a generic statement of “Please enter in Katakana” is displayed for SC, TC and KR languages when inputting an invalid input in the Kana fields.



Steps to Reproduce:

# Open [https://stg.reservation.tokyustay.co.jp/en|https://stg.reservation.tokyustay.co.jp/en] > Set page language to either TC, SC or KR
# Go to Edit Profile
# Change the user’s Country to Japan
# In the First Name(Kana) or Last Name(Kana) fields, enter any input that is NOT Katakana characters ((such as *alphabets, numbers, special characters or Hiragana characters*)
# Click “Save Changes”



Current Result:

Error message does not state "Please enter in Katakana" when user enters invalid input into First Name(Kana) & Last Name(Kana) fields  when page language is TC, SC or KR and user country is JP



Expected Result:

Error message specifically instructs the user to “Please input in Katakana”.

It is observed that when comparing fields in *Edit Profile* and *Reservation Confirmation* screens, there are 2 types of input validation methods that are used when user attempts to enter characters above a field’s maximum allowed limit.



Validation {color:#bf2600}*Method #1*{color}*:* 

* Restrict the user from entering any more characters once they reach the maximum limit for the field



Validation {color:#ff991f}*Method #2*{color}*:*

* Allow the user to enter more characters than the maximum limit. When the user exceeds the maximum limit or presses the relevant button to “Confirm” their input, the user is displayed an error message to “Please enter a valid input / Please enter a maximum of X characters”



However, only the *Phone Number* field is observed to be using Validation {color:#ff991f}*Method #2*{color}. Ideally, it would be better to have the Phone Number field in both *Edit Profile* & *Reservation Confirmation* screen field use Validation {color:#bf2600}*Method #1* {color}so that it is consistent with the other fields validation methods.



Additionally, it is mentioned in this [ticket|https://jitera.atlassian.net/browse/TS-1771] as per a discussion in our DSU that for the maximum limit for all fields, the *system should not allow the user to enter more than the maximum character limit.*

Error message is not clear when user attempts to confirm reservation with specific invalid email formats. 

The error message shown states “Something went wrong on submitting your reservation”. Due to this, the user most likely won’t know that the issue is with their email format as there is no indication that the email format is invalid.



+List of invalid email formats (Example):+

* a@b
* a@b.c
* a@b.com

*Note:* For the prefix, “a” and the domain name, “b”, you can enter any value and it gives the same error. 



Steps to Reproduce:

# Open [https://stg.reservation.tokyustay.co.jp/ja|https://stg.reservation.tokyustay.co.jp/ja] > Login
# Select any Hotel > Select any check-in & check-out date > Search
# Select “Book Now” on any hotel room.
# In the email field, enter any one of the invalid email formats listed above
# Fill in valid inputs in all other fields > Click “Confirm” button.



Current Result:

Error message is not clear when user attempts to confirm reservation with specific invalid email formats.


Expected Result:

Error message mentions clearly that the error is due to invalid email format entered by the user.

Note: This is a suggested Improvement ticket.

When the user clicks the “Yes, Cancel” button in the Cancel Reservation pop-up menu, the part of the button turns blank white. Since it takes a while for the cancellation process to complete, it gives the impression to the user that the app may be unresponsive since there is no indication that the cancellation process is in progress.

To improve the user experience, it is suggested to add a “Spinner” icon or any UI element to inform the user that the cancellation process is currently in progress.
